The working tree in this container is not at the reviewed head, so every citation below is from `git show` of the head's tree; nothing was built, run or re-run. The `check:ci-filter-parity` gate runs in `lint.yml`'s `lint-ci-engine` job (`Lint · CI, release & engine gates`), which is `success` on the head, so the self-test's 138 assertions and the three OK lines are the check-run's answer, not the PR body's.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set change the diff implies, each judged against the head's tree:

1. **A diff confined to the root `package.json` now starts the six PR-time ui jobs — right.** `.github/actions/setup-pnpm/action.yml` resolves the pin with `node -p "require('$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/package.json').packageManager ?? ''"` and exits 1 without it. `ui-deps`, `type-check-ui`, `test-ui`, `lint-ui`, `build-e2e-ui` and `live-e2e-ui` each `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm` directly (and `ui-published-artifacts` on push). `test-ui` and `lint-ui` read `needs.filter.outputs.ui` alone, so `ui_consumers` cannot start them and `core` reaches only `live-e2e-ui`: `ui:` is the narrowest list that starts all six, as the card's Wanted asks. Before the diff the `ui:` list carried no `package.json` row; now it carries exactly one.
2. **A diff confined to the root `package.json` now starts Build Docs — right, and inside the card.** `build-docs` is gated on `needs.filter.outputs.docs != 'false'` and its first step after checkout is `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-workspace`, whose second step is `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm`. The card's Wanted names "the narrowest list whose jobs run `setup-pnpm`"; Build Docs runs it, and `docs:` is the only list that schedules Build Docs. The `docs:` list had no `package.json` row before; it has one now, beside the three #27673 rows it already carried for the same reason.
3. **A diff confined to one of the five generic `test` inputs now starts `test-plan` and `test` (Test Core) — right.** turbo.json's generic `test` task carries eight `$TURBO_ROOT$` inputs; `vitest.preset.mts` was already a literal `core:` row, `ui/scripts/vite-*.ts` and `ui/scripts/vitest-invocation-guard.mjs` are literal `core:` build rows, and the remaining five (`ui/vitest.config.mts`, `ui/vitest.setup.*`, `ui/scripts/test-shard-*`, `ui/apps/console/vitest.config.ts`, `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts`) matched nothing in `core` or `crosspkg` before and are now verbatim `core:` rows. Both `test-plan` and `test` read `core != 'false' || crosspkg != 'false'`. Each glob names real files in the head's tree (nine `ui/vitest.setup.*` files, three `ui/scripts/test-shard-*` files, the two Console configs, `ui/vitest.config.mts`). There is no generic `test:repo` task in turbo.json, so the population is exactly these eight, which is the "all 8 root input(s)" the OK line reports.
4. **Side effect of 3, named rather than hidden:** a `core:` row starts the whole core pipeline (Build Core, Live E2E UI's core clause, and on push the temporal and dogfood legs) on a diff to, say, `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts`. That is the price of every `core:` row and the one the parity gate's own leftover text names; it is the ruling's shape (6513291766 letter A, the six build inputs) one task over, and the triage on #27961 reads it as the same shape. The PR body's 30-day replay figures (ui +11, docs +18, core +2 of 3683 commits) are the dev's measurement and were not re-derived here.
5. **Nothing previously scheduled is now skipped — right.** `ci.yml` is 23 additions and 0 deletions; every existing row and every job `if:` is unchanged. `lint.yml` changes one step's name, comment lines and final `echo` text; the step `id` `scripts-shared-module-self-tests-parse-entry`, its `continue-on-error`, its collector shape and its five `run_self_test` lines are unchanged.
6. **Public surface — none.** No `packages/**` file changes. The parity script gains exported symbols (`TEST_TASKS`, `TEST_REMEDY_FILTER`, `testInputsOf`, `judgeTestInputs`) and new OK/FAIL text, but it is a root `scripts/` gate whose only consumer is `lint.yml`'s `pnpm check:ci-filter-parity` step and its own self-test. Nothing outside `lint.yml` reads the renamed step's name or its final line: `git grep` on the head for `all four ran`, `every one ran`, `shared-module self-tests (parse` and the step id outside `lint.yml` returns only unrelated ui test prose.

### ② Semver level

The PR body's `Clause-②: no` line and the `skip-changeset` label match what the diff publishes: nothing. The three files are a governed workflow, a second governed workflow and a root repository gate; no package manifest, source or `.changeset/` file is touched, and `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head. Not a narrowing: no declared capability is taken away at any consumer. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report `open_questions`: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- Dev report deviation 1, the `docs:` row as a "declared increment": answered in ①.2 — it is inside the card's own Wanted ("the narrowest list whose jobs run `setup-pnpm`"), the same gate family and the same file; it adds a schedule and removes none. Not an escalation.
- Dev report deviation 2 (model-free commit trailers) and 3 (report posted on the chain head only): housekeeping, not a contract matter.
- Card #27961 Wanted 1 asked for a maintainer letter between route A (a fourth parity subject plus the five rows) and route B (a recorded decision not to follow generic test inputs). Triage 6516081082 answered that item 1 inherits ruling 6513291766 (letter A, maintainer 「其他同意」) and adds no gate. The PR takes route A as ruled; this record does not re-open the letter.
- Card #27961's acceptance is "a diff confined to one of the five starts Test Core on the PR". The rows make `test-plan` and `test` eligible; which packages the plan then bins is `scripts/ci/select-shard-packages.sh`'s `turbo ls --affected` unioned with the cross-package declarations, which this PR does not touch and the PR body says it did not measure. That is the same bound ruling 6513291766 accepted for the six build rows, and the card's Measured names "only the timing of Test Core's first run" as the defect. Noted, not escalated: it is outside both cards' file surface and the ruling's shape.
- Tier H: the diff touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, so the maintainer's approving review is still owed on the PR and is whole-PR; this record is the contract review, not that approval. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards` are `success` on the head.
- No gate on the head is `failure`; no derived family is unmeasured.

### ④ Design judgment

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — held against the code it cites. (i) The `ui:` and `docs:` comments say setup-pnpm reads `packageManager` from the root manifest: it does, at the first step of the composite action, and fails the job when the field is absent, so a pnpm bump that reaches `main` with the ui jobs skipped is exactly the gap #27673 closed for `.nvmrc`. (ii) The `core:` comment says the five rows are the generic `test` task's `$TURBO_ROOT$` inputs and that "`vitest.preset.mts` above and the `vite-*.ts` / `vitest-invocation-guard.mjs` build rows cover the other three": true against the head's turbo.json, whose `test` task carries exactly those eight and whose `core:` list carries the three literal rows named. (iii) Tried to break it: the rows are byte-identical to the turbo inputs minus the `$TURBO_ROOT$/` prefix, which is what the gate's pure-string coverage rule requires (a literal match or a `prefix/**` subtree; no glob expansion), so a future spelling drift reds rather than silently un-covers. `ui/scripts/test-shard-*` also matches `ui/scripts/test-shard-timings.json`; turbo hashes the same file under the same glob, so the schedule and the hash move together. No row was added to a list that already carried it; no `if:` changed. Holds.

**`.github/workflows/lint.yml`** — held against the step it describes. The step runs five `run_self_test` lines (`scripts/ts-parse.mjs`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, `ui/scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, `scripts/import-prerequisite.mjs`); the new name lists parse · entry predicate, root and ui · comment mask · prerequisite frame, which is those five; the comment no longer says "four" anywhere, explains why the ui twin sits in this step (it is a `core:` build input, so `check:self-test-wired` counts it, and its `--self-test` ran nowhere else — true against the head's `core:` list), and the final line pins no count. `node scripts/check-step-collectors.mjs` extracts this block by file and drives it under `bash -e`; its lint lane is `success` on the head. "~0.9 s combined" is the dev's re-measurement and is harmless either way. Holds.

**`scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs`** — the gate the rules cite, read (not reviewed) to judge the two rows above. `judgeTestInputs` reuses `readSchedulingFilters`, so it inherits the first subject's refusals (no `filter` job, not exactly one `dorny/paths-filter` step, a `test` job whose `if:` stops naming `core` or `crosspkg`), and adds its own for turbo.json unreadable, not JSON, no `tasks` map, and no generic `test` task; the five refusal cases in battery (11) drive each. `testInputsOf` takes only string inputs beginning `$TURBO_ROOT$/`, so a negation (`!$TURBO_ROOT$/...`) and a `pkg#test` task fall out by construction, and the self-test pins both. `main()` and `list()` both wire the new verdict and the return code ANDs it in, so one red never hides another. The leftover rule's `reasons` now include `testInputsOf(turbo).rows ?? []`: a turbo.json without a generic `test` task yields a refusal object whose `rows` is undefined, so the fallback shrinks the reasons and reports more, never less, as the comment says; and `reasonDirs` now includes `ui/apps/console`, so a literal `core:` row placed there that covers no reason reds — the right direction. Battery (11) registers eighteen assertions, matching its declared floor of 18; the roster floor moves 9 to 10 with the roster at ten entries. The task-pair bound's regex matches the whole-package leg (`pnpm turbo run test test:repo $FILTERS`) and not the slice leg (`pnpm turbo run test "--filter=$PKG"`), because the latter has no `$FILTERS` token, so the bound pins exactly the pair that defines the population. The header's bound paragraph now names setup-workspace: Build Core's only local composite action is `./.github/actions/setup-workspace`, whose `run:` steps call `pnpm store path` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and the setup-pnpm it calls runs `node -p`, `corepack`, `pnpm --version` and a store assertion — no repository script in either, and `.nvmrc`, both action directories and `package.json` are `core:` rows. Holds.

**Findings.**

- Must-fix: none.
- Should-fix (a card, not this PR): no gate holds the new `ui:` and `docs:` `package.json` rows, exactly as none holds #27673's `.nvmrc` and setup-action rows in those lists — the parity gate's subjects are Test Core and Build Core, and `ui/scripts/__tests__/ci-setup-pnpm-wiring.test.ts` pins the ui jobs' steps, not the `ui:` filter list. A row dropped later reds nothing. Out of both cards' Wanted.
- Should-fix (a card, not this PR): two pre-existing prose counts are now stale for the same reason #27961 item 2 was — `ci.yml`'s ui-section note ("these five jobs keep the setup steps spelled out") and `setup-workspace/action.yml`'s header ("ci.yml's five ui jobs" use setup-pnpm directly) both undercount; seven `ci.yml` jobs `uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm` directly on the head. Neither line is in this PR's hunks.
